caption: Floor: a smooth palette sweep rounded down into eight flat bands of colour
why: Rounding down turns a smooth number into steps: 2.7 becomes 2. That makes cells out of a coordinate (which column, which tile), stepped colour out of a gradient, and frame-by-frame jumps out of a clock.
Its neighbours: Fract keeps the part after the point (Floor keeps the part before); Map range with steps rounds to a number of steps; Hash turns the whole numbers Floor makes into randoms.
steps: Floor rounds it down: 0 for the first eighth of the matrix, 1 for the next, up to 7 - eight flat steps.
Divided by 8 (a **Multiply** by 0.125) plus a clock (**Time** times 0.15) it is the **Palette**'s index: eight flat bands of colour, each one solid, all shifting together.
Without the Floor, the colours would blend smoothly across.

try.label: Three bands
try.text: the first Multiply at 3 and the second at 0.333: three wide bands.

try.label: Sixteen
try.text: the first Multiply at 16 and the second at 0.0625: sixteen narrow bands - nearly smooth again.
